However both impact legs collapse: (a) every real status surface the finding names re-resolves READY against GameState and shows the truth - ArenaCommand.java:115-117 + getArenaStatus:171 renders "arena-status-ending", ArenaManageGUI.java:972-982 does the same, ArenaSelectionGUI.java:205 does the same - and ArenaStatus.java:4-8 documents that a READY arena's GameState may be any value, so READY is a lifecycle (loaded/not-disabled) flag, not a joinability promise; (b) `/hilltop enable` is not and never was the repair path: MultiArenaManager.enableArena itself early-returns true at 286-288 whenever activeArenas contains the id, so bypassing the handler's pre-check at HilltopCommandHandler.java:1416 would produce the same no-op while falsely reporting "queued". Recovery is neither hidden nor trial-and-error: the very log line at ArenaInstance.java:1436 tells the admin to run `/hilltop disable` then `/hilltop enable` (disableArena:450-463 permits ENDING and removes the instance, so the enable then really rebuilds it), `/hilltop stop` (HilltopCommandHandler.java:253) calls stopGame()->scheduleReset()->reset() which re-issues restoreWithResult with the blocks requeued at MapRestoreManager.java:699-707/728, and a restart clears it.
